questions.question: Explain the difference between lines of latitude and lines of longitude.
questions.expected_answer: Lines of latitude run across the globe from west to east, are parallel to the equator and never meet. They measure how far north or south of the equator a place is, from zero to ninety degrees. Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole, meet at the poles and measure how far east or west of the Greenwich Meridian a place is, from zero to one hundred and eighty degrees.

questions.question: Name the special lines of latitude and give their approximate degrees.
questions.expected_answer: The equator is at zero degrees. The Tropic of Cancer is at about twenty-three and a half degrees north, and the Tropic of Capricorn at about twenty-three and a half degrees south. The Arctic Circle is at about sixty-six and a half degrees north, and the Antarctic Circle at about sixty-six and a half degrees south.

questions.question: Why must a latitude always say north or south, and a longitude always say east or west?
questions.expected_answer: The same number of degrees exists on both sides of the starting line. Twenty-four degrees could be north or south of the equator, and twenty-nine degrees could be east or west of Greenwich, so without the direction we would not know which place is meant.
